title: Throughput-constrained hiring waterfall and pricing hedge
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet prototypes a waterfall-style hiring plan tied to throughput (tokens/sec) and a complementary pricing hedge that activates price guardrails when capacity utilization and token demand diverge. Intended as a lightweight, actionable model for Finance + Capacity to use when demand signals spike or degrade. Not final — assumptions called out below.

Key assumptions (base):
- Current steady-state throughput target: 1.2M tokens/sec global (avg across regions).
- Baseline on-demand GPU pool: 120 GPU-equivalents (mix of A100/RTX8000 style).
- Avg tokens per call: 1,200; 30% streaming/long-tail.
- Backend lead time for hiring infra/operators: 8–12 weeks per hire (avg 10w).
- Avg fully-burdened SRE/Infra engineer cost: $28k/month (incl payroll burden, benefits, tax).
- Rapid-contract/consultant cost: 1.8x salary equivalent for short bursts.
- Price elasticity estimate: 3% drop in usage per 1% price increase for downstream high-volume customers (sensitivity band).

Waterfall hiring plan (runnable cells):
Columns: Step | Trigger (util % sustained 7d) | Quantity (FTE or GPUs) | Ramp lead (weeks) | Monthly runrate delta 
1 | 75% util sustained | +10 GPU equiv (spot to reserved mix) | 1 week procurement/burst | $40k 
2 | 85% util sustained OR queuing >50ms p95 | +6 infra FTE (ops/oncall) | 10 weeks hire/ramp | $168k 
3 | 92% util sustained AND forecasted demand +15% over 30d | +30 GPU equiv (reserved commit) | 6 weeks from exec ok | $120k 
4 | 95% util + risk-of-degradation | +external-burst contractor pool (12 FTE-eq) | immediate (contract) | $240k 
Notes: GPU equiv costs include amortized cloud/spot/reserved blended cost. Revise based on regional pricing.

Pricing hedge / guardrail rules (proposed automation knobs):
- Soft-tilt (automated): If p95 latency > target AND util > 80% for 72h, increase routed-price (quote multiplier) to new customers by +6% on On-Demand plan for 7 days.
- Hard-tilt (manual escalation): If util > 92% and error-rate impact observed, trigger canary of per-route price uplift (+12%) for top 10% of token-consuming routes and pause free-tier bursting.
- Customer protections: Tiered warning emails at +20% bill forecast and offer optional smoothing credits for committed customers.
- Elasticity fallback: On hard tilt, estimate revenue delta from uplift vs. churn risk using elasticities.

Scenario matrix (base / surge / contraction):
- Base: demand growth +2%/mo; hiring waterfall only uses Step 1; price unchanged; runway unaffected.
- Surge: sudden +40% demand (marketing/customer onboarding) over 14d. Triggers Step 1->3 and activates contractor pool. Pricing soft-tilt applied to non-committed tenants. Net effect: incremental cost +$420k/mo for first 2 months; expected revenue retention 88% (12% churn among non-committed).
- Contraction: -18% demand over 30d; defer reserved commits, shift to spot; headcount hiring frozen; potential price rollback incentive to retain committed customers.

Model outputs (example cells / outputs):
- Monthly marginal cost per 1% demand delta: $14.5k (computed from blended GPU and ops runrate)
- Breakeven price uplift required to offset +25% throughput demand: ~9.8% (given elasticity assumption)
- Lead-time risk buffer (weeks): 10w typical hire ramp -> keep 20% surge headroom as planning buffer

Practical playbook (action items):
1) Finance to publish "surge cost escrow" of $600k for up to 8 weeks of contractor+spot usage; runway gating to Exec signoff if escalation expected beyond month 2.
2) Ops to build a realtime dashboard: util p95, open slots (GPU equiv), queued requests, top 20 token consumers.
3) RevOps to draft default temporary price-tilt messaging and customer credits policy.
4) People ops to prepare expedited hiring pipeline (interviews, contractor agencies list) for infra hires.

Open questions / risks:
- Elasticity is noisy by segment — need route-level historical elasticity estimation to avoid overpricing vulnerable customers.
- Reserved commit cancellation windows and penalties vary by cloud vendor; model to be updated with vendor-specific amortization schedules.
- On-prem/private customers not price-tied — need separate capacity assurance runbook.

Appendix (quick calc snippets):
- Incremental cost = (Delta GPUs * blended GPU $/month) + (Delta FTE * FTE $/month) + contractor premium.
- Example: +30 GPUs at $4k/gpu/mo = $120k; +6 FTE at $28k/mo = $168k; contractor cover (12 FTE-eq at 1.8x) = $240k -> total first-month hit = $528k.
- Price uplift breakeven: Required uplift % = incremental_cost / (expected_additional_revenue_base * (1 - elasticity_effect)). Use route-level revenue base where possible.

Next steps (short):
- Validate assumptions with SRE (GPU blended cost, procurement lead-times) by 2026-02-28.
- Run a 12-week simulated surge in the capacity model repo (linked) and capture sensitivity to elasticity bands [0.5, 1.0, 3.0].
- Convert key cells to a live Google Sheet and wire to dashboards for automatic triggers (Ops + Finance).

Author notes: draft intended for cross-functional review. Please annotate cells you want to preserve vs. replace with vendor-specific numbers.
